doc.title: Nancy Wilson — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: School grades and an early taste for suits
summary: She was an A student except for geometry and home ec, and says she has always preferred suits and trousers to dresses.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: School days: grades, teachers and leaving school

blocks.x: Were you good in school? Did you like school?
I was an A student. I think I got one C.

Probably home economics. Something like that. I’m trying to remember what it was. Oh, I remember: geometry. I had A’s in algebra, but I got a C in geometry. And I never did finish the blouse I was working on in home ec.
Who got you ready for school?
Later we’re going to get into your sense of style. I was wondering how early it started?

I don’t remember not being the way I am. I’ve always been suits, trousers, sports jackets. I love great suits. I never was a skirt-wearing person. Don’t have great legs. Have a great body from the knee up. But the legs are not that great. So I never really liked dresses.
